The uric acid level is normal, which effectively rules out an acute gout attack as the primary cause of your current pain. The X-ray findings of joint space narrowing and osteophyte formation in your hips and knees are classic signs of osteoarthritis, and while gout can affect the great toe, the structural damage seen in your other joints points strongly to degenerative disease as the main diagnosis.
